Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, focal enhancement within the same area. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone lesions are seen within the field of view.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: 16 Jan 2023 - Dr. L. Smits (GP): Patient presented with elevated PSA of 4.4 ng/mL on screening. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy was performed. Histology returned as Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. Patient was counselled on active surveillance versus treatment options. Referred to urology for multidisciplinary discussion.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: 10 May 2024 - Dr. L. Smits (GP): Routine follow-up visit. PSA has risen to 9.0 ng/mL. Patient reports no new urinary or systemic symptoms. Repeat prostate biopsy was arranged. Results show persistent Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. Patient remains stable clinically. Referred to urology for re-evaluation of management strategy.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (16 Jan 2023): Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. No perineural invasion is present.

Biopsy 2 (10 May 2024): Repeat prostate biopsy demonstrates adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. No perineural invasion is observed.

Summary: The histological grade remains stable across both biopsy timepoints.
